title: tidy lists every recorded leftover with one safe_to_remove verdict, reason and bytes, and --apply removes only the safe set
goal: bl_clean.safe_to_remove(candidate, snapshot, coord_state) returns (verdict, reason) and is the one function tidy, kbmon and the remediation agent call; a candidate is removable only when its owner is recorded, no live coord lease or claim names it or its branch or item, no live process has it as its working directory, its item is done or dropped or gone with its closed sprint, it is clean and merged into origin/main, with its last activity older than --older-than HOURS (default 4); backlog.py tidy lists each recorded worktree, local branch, bench sandbox and scratch directory with that verdict, its reason and the bytes it frees, one summary line per class, and --json prints the same rows; the main checkout, the worktree tidy runs in, _cache/querylog/worktree and everything no record names are always kept; --apply removes the safe set with git worktree remove (never --force), deletes a branch only when git cherry finds its commits on origin/main, then runs git worktree prune, under the operator's answer to gate g1; a directory Windows refuses to rename is kept and reported, never forced; under disk pressure (free space below --disk-free-gb) bench sandboxes are listed first with their age limit waived

import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, json, time
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
ENV = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(("GIT_", "KB_COORD"))}
ENV.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)
ENV.update(KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(T, "coord.sqlite"), GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM="1",
           GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
def g(*a, cwd):
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=cwd, env=ENV, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
def tool(*a, env=None, ok=(0,)):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=env or ENV, timeout=300)
    assert r.returncode in ok, (a, r.returncode, r.stdout[-800:], r.stderr[-800:])
    return r
O, C = os.path.join(T, "origin.git"), os.path.join(T, "clone")
g("init", "-q", "--bare", "-b", "main", O, cwd=T)
g("clone", "-q", O, C, cwd=T)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog"))
open(os.path.join(C, "backlog.json"), "w").write('{"item_dir": "kb/_self/backlog"}\n')
open(os.path.join(C, "kb", "_self", "backlog", ".keep"), "w").close()
g("add", "-A", cwd=C); g("commit", "-qm", "base", cwd=C); g("push", "-q", "origin", "main", cwd=C); g("fetch", "-q", cwd=C)
WT = os.path.join(C, ".claude", "worktrees")
def wt(name, branch=None, at="HEAD"):
    p = os.path.join(WT, name)
    g("worktree", "add", "-q", *(["-b", branch] if branch else ["--detach"]), p, at, cwd=C)
    return p
n = lambda p: os.path.normcase(os.path.realpath(p))
def own(p, cls, *a, env=None):
    return tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "own", str(p), "--class", cls, *a, env=env)
def rows(*a):
    return json.loads(tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--json", *a).stdout)
def by_path(rs, cls=None):
    return {n(x["path"]): x for x in rs if "path" in x and (cls is None or x.get("class") == cls)}
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
try:
    import bl_clean
except ImportError:
    bl_clean = None
assert callable(getattr(bl_clean, "safe_to_remove", None)), "no bl_clean.safe_to_remove"
S = ENV["KB_COORD_STORE"]
ok = wt("agent-ok", "work/ST-aaaaaaaa"); own(ok, "worktree", "--item", "ST-aaaaaaaa")
dirty = wt("agent-dirty", "work/ST-bbbbbbbb"); own(dirty, "worktree", "--item", "ST-bbbbbbbb")
open(os.path.join(dirty, "new.txt"), "w").write("x")
unm = wt("agent-unmerged", "work/ST-cccccccc"); own(unm, "worktree", "--item", "ST-cccccccc")
open(os.path.join(unm, "f.txt"), "w").write("x"); g("add", "f.txt", cwd=unm); g("commit", "-qm", "unmerged", cwd=unm)
foreign = wt("agent-foreign", "work/ST-dddddddd")
busy = wt("agent-busy", "work/ST-eeeeeeee"); own(busy, "worktree", "--item", "ST-eeeeeeee")
P = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(600)"], cwd=busy)
lease = wt("agent-lease", "work/ST-ffffffff"); own(lease, "worktree", "--item", "ST-ffffffff", "--session", "s-live")
tool("_tools/coord.py", "--store", S, "claim", "session/s-live", "--ttl", "600")
ql = os.path.join(C, "_cache", "querylog", "worktree"); g("worktree", "add", "-q", "--detach", ql, "HEAD", cwd=C); own(ql, "worktree")
try:
    v = by_path(rows(), "worktree")
    assert v[n(ok)]["verdict"] == "keep" and "4" in v[n(ok)]["reason"], ("the default age limit of 4 hours", v[n(ok)])
    v = by_path(rows("--older-than", "0"), "worktree")
    want = {ok: None, dirty: "uncommitted", unm: "lacks", foreign: "no owner record", busy: "process", lease: "lease",
            ql: "query log"}
    for p, word in want.items():
        x = v.get(n(p)); assert x, (p, sorted(v))
        if word is None:
            assert x["verdict"] == "remove" and isinstance(x.get("bytes"), int), x
        else:
            assert x["verdict"] == "keep" and word in x["reason"], (p, x)
    r = tool("_tools/backlog.py", "--root", C, "tidy", "--older-than", "0")
    assert any(ln.startswith("tidy: worktree") for ln in r.stdout.splitlines()), ("no summary line per class", r.stdout)
    assert all(os.path.isdir(p) for p in want), "a dry run removed something"
finally:
    P.kill()

gates.question: Agent shells are denied git worktree remove and git branch -D (.claude/settings.json). How may tidy's removal of worktrees and local branches run without getting around that rule? Note: the allow rule Bash(python3 _tools/backlog.py *) already lets agent sessions run tidy --apply, land and close, which run those git commands as their own processes (bl_land.release_worker_worktree, delete_landed_branch); the answer also says whether today's tidy --apply gets the same refusal.
options: operator-run: tidy --apply refuses in a Claude Code session (bl_authority.in_agent_session); the operator runs it in a terminal of their own or installs a scheduled run (cron, launchd or Task Scheduler) outside agent sessions; land and close keep only the removal of their own items' worker worktrees they do today

narrow allow: the operator records a decision that agent sessions may run exactly python3 _tools/backlog.py tidy --apply, which removes only what safe_to_remove proves finished and owned; every other removal stays operator-run
as the narrow allow, and land and close also call it for their own recorded leftovers (orchestrator and reviewer worktrees, scratch)

notes: Test policy (D-6kei5o2z, D-2tq4fhgs): no new test or test file; the checks are tool runs on a throwaway clone with planted inputs (KB_COORD_STORE points at its own coord store, so no check writes the clone's real one); no change to _tools/tests_ceiling.json. Reuses from the operator's one-off cleanup.sh: dry run by default and --apply to act; never --force; skip a dirty worktree, one with untracked files, one a process sits in, one whose HEAD is not in origin/main; always keep the main checkout and _cache/querylog/worktree; git worktree prune afterwards. Reuses from tidy and bl_land: tidy_worktree_kept, release_worker_worktree, delete_landed_branch, live_processes (lsof/proc) and held_by_process (Windows rename). cmd_tidy and its registration move from bl_land.py to bl_clean.py; tidy's name rule (any agent-* worktree, orch/* branch) goes, per the operator's records-only answer. Premise (2026-10-19, this host): git worktree list shows 50 worktrees, of which tidy today would remove 0 and keeps 18 branches; 846 code/* branches on origin, all merged. Last activity, measured on this host 2026-10-19: a worktree's index file time is rewritten by any git status (tidy's own clean check included; use git --no-optional-locks), and every worktree's logs/HEAD file time was rewritten at once by a gc; the newest HEAD reflog entry's own time (git log -g -1 --format=%ct) is the reliable figure. A dry run of the operator's one-time script with these rules found 36 of 49 worktrees removable (34 rebase-landed planning worktrees, so the merged test is git cherry, not merge-base --is-ancestor) and kept two worktrees of a sprint that had closed minutes before only by their recent activity: a record plus the coord lease covers that case in tidy.
